Hi Samir,

Great to meet you and Jill on the call today — thanks for walking through Acme's ingestion and moderation flows. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

- Summary of needs: high-throughput summarization for customer support tickets, strict PII redaction, and consistent tone for public responses.
- Success metrics you shared: <=200ms median latency for 512-token responses, F1 >=0.88 on entity-redaction tests, and <2% regression vs current quality baseline.

Recommended next steps: 
1) Prompt/edge-case collection: please share 20-30 representative prompts (real or redacted) covering typical tickets, noisy transcripts, and expected failure modes (e.g., nested PII, long threads). We can ingest these into our eval harness.
2) Model & eval plan: we'll run a 3-model mini-benchmark (latency/cost/quality) and propose a production variant. Expect results in ~3 business days after we receive prompts.
3) Security/compliance: you flagged retention and redaction rules — I've attached a short checklist and forwarded your security questionnaire to our Trust team.

Attachments: acme_security_questionnaire.pdf (you can also upload to the Drive link below).

Links: benchmark folder: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/benchmark-acme-2026
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/123456789

Thanks —

Thanks for the clear recap. Attaching a first pass — anonymized — of ~25 prompts (acme_sample_prompts.csv) and a short text file with examples and notes (acme_prompt_examples.txt). Highlights/concerns: 

- Many of our tickets contain multiple customer identifiers (email, acct#, phone) and free-text agent notes with quoted sections.
- We often need to redact embedded addresses and order numbers that look like structured tokens (e.g., ORD-12345).
- Some long threads include bot/system messages that should be ignored by the model.
- We want to avoid quality regressions that change policy language (e.g., refund reasons) — stability on those templates is critical.

Subject: Re: Redwood Eval + Prompt Collection — Model candidates & initial results

Hi Samir / Marissa,

I ran a quick 3-model mini-benchmark using the sample prompts you provided. Top-level findings (full artifact in the Drive folder):

- Latency (512 tokens, p50): RedMod-13B-Prod = 95ms, Mistral-Instruct-70B (quant) = 180ms, Llama-3-70b-q4 = 210ms (on our dedicated 8xA100 pool).
- Redaction recall (entity removal tests): Llama-3-70b-q4 = 0.92, Mistral-Instruct-70B = 0.88, RedMod-13B-Prod = 0.85.
- Quality (fidelity to policy templates / classification tests): Llama-3-70b-q4 and Mistral both meet your F1 target on the sampled templates; RedMod occasionally rewrites boilerplate language — recommend guardrails if used.
- Cost: RedMod-13B most cost-effective per-token; Llama-70B higher throughput cost.

Recommendations: 
1) For lowest latency + cost with acceptable redaction: start with RedMod-13B-Prod and enable prefix/KV caching for thread-summary flows. Add a small supervised safety post-process for policy-critical templates to avoid wording regressions.
2) If you need stricter PII removal out-of-the-box, Llama-3-70b-q4 is the strongest candidate and we can run targeted fine-tune/adapter tests.
3) We'll produce a short A/B plan: RedMod baseline + Llama safety variant for canary rollout.

Action items for Samir: please confirm which of the following you prefer for the eval deliverable: 
- Full scored CSV (per-prompt metrics) + example outputs
- Live demo session to walk through edge cases
- Both (we usually do both for enterprise).

I'll upload the detailed CSV and a short README to the Drive folder by EOD.

Thanks,
Aditya
